Biezun Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bieżuń, Poland

Demolished. Bieżuń, founded under Chełmno law in 1406, saw Jewish settlement begin in the early 18th century, with a first wooden synagogue built after 1760; population grew from 389 (1808) to 697 by 1857 (boosted by Jews expelled from Mława), settling at 779 by 1921. Notable native son Izaak Cylkow (b. 1841), a renowned rabbi and Torah translator into Polish, was born there. Wartime deportations sent residents through Mława, Szreńsk, and Strzegowo before reaching Auschwitz and Treblinka. This cemetery, established either at the end of the 18th or beginning of the 19th century, received its last burial in 1940 before wartime devastation repurposed matzevot for street paving. A 2014 plaque, initiated by Herman Storick and the Cmentarze-zydowskie.pl team, reads: 'Jewish Cemetery. Please respect the burial place of the inhabitants of your town.'
